chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a group for whom one cow would suffice,
He said: As for the hady, no; but as for the uḍḥiyah, yes.

Another possible interpretation is that this was only allowed in a state of necessity and not in a state of choice; and there has already appeared, throughout these reports, that which indicates this and clarifies it further.

key_terms.الضَّرُورَةِ: a state of necessity or compulsion
key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةِ: the ritual sacrifice offered as uḍḥiyah
key_terms.الْهَدْيِ: the sacrificial offering connected to hajj rites

ai.seo_question: Can one cow suffice for several people in hady or uḍḥiyah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between sacrificial rulings: a cow does not suffice on behalf of multiple people in the hady offered at Minā, but it does suffice in the uḍḥiyah. The compiler then notes another possible reconciliation, namely that such allowance may apply only in cases of necessity rather than free choice.
